coverage_gaps: No person-specific event involving a covered right-wing, Republican, conservative, or affiliated-organizational figure was located in Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, or Missouri that met the evidence and date-window rules.

Ohio, Illinois, Missouri, Minnesota, Iowa, Wisconsin, and federal official indexes reviewed showed no qualifying new covered-person misconduct action in the window; the newest visible releases were generally dated August 14 or earlier, or concerned private defendants and ordinary public employees without documented covered political affiliation.

The Illinois Attorney General items dated August 11-14 involved a former sheriff employee or private defendants and did not document a covered right-wing or Republican role; they were outside the lookback or failed the affiliation rule and were excluded.

Indiana and Michigan press-release and court indexes use dynamic or partially searchable interfaces, and local police, sheriff, prosecutor, court, school-board, municipal, and ethics records are fragmented rather than exposed through one statewide index.

Several major regional-news domains were blocked by robots.txt. A Madison police-monitor discussion surfaced in social results, but it was outside the window, lacked documented covered political affiliation, and was not used as evidence or retained as a quarantine lead.
